summary: Round 2 passes with one Major and two Nits. HEAD equals the audited head. The commit closes F17 to F22 with exact commands, an exact message, the Phase 1 fixtures on master, and the three test files. The Major: row 22(b), a present fork-only commit, cannot be built with the one master fetch, because the script's scratch repository is private and loads no fork ref; the spec must delete the row or name the second refspec. Route to the author.

paraphrase.proposes: The revised amendment keeps the one non-shallow, blobless `master` fetch and drops the fetch of the release commit by SHA. The script then runs `git cat-file -e` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; an absent commit or a non-ancestor stops with one exact line. Criterion 22 has an absent row and an optional present row, and criterion 23 passes an old non-tip commit of `master`.
paraphrase.current_system: The Phase 1 script fetches the release commit by its SHA with `--depth=1 --filter=blob:none`, then compares the upload with that commit. It carries no check that the upstream `master` holds the commit, so it accepts a commit that exists only in a fork. The runbook tells the operator to pass the release commit, and the push path uses a separate SHA-256 manifest.

nonblocking_findings: F23 [Major] spec.md:207, :212 and plan.md:70: row 22(b), a present fork-only commit, cannot be built with the method of section 8.2. The script's scratch repository is a private `mktemp -d` that fetches only `master`, so every present commit is an ancestor of `FETCH_HEAD`, and the test cannot place the fork-only object there; the `refs/pull/<n>/head` object stays in the fixture repository. The spec calls the row optional and says it `stands only when the fetch names a second ref`, but section 8.2 names no second ref. Rationale: the implementer must choose between dropping the row and adding a second refspec such as `+refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/pull/*`, and the merge-base exit-1 branch stays untested. The spec must state one choice.

F24 [Nit] spec.md:194: the sentence `the release commit is a commit of master, so this one fetch holds it` presupposes the result of the check. The fetch holds the commit only when the check passes. Rationale: step 2 of :195 handles the absence, so the method is clear, but a reader can take the sentence as a guarantee.

F25 [Nit] spec.md:196 and plan.md:71: a tool failure `stops with its own message`, but the text fixes no literal and no criterion asserts it. Rationale: the implementer chooses the text of the edge-case message; the build behavior does not change.

The fork-only commit sits on `refs/pull/<n>/head` (spec.md:212) and is not fetched. A test cannot seed the scratch repository, so row 22(b) at spec.md:207 and plan.md:70 is unbuildable as written.
